summary: Root cause is a breaking event-schema change deployed by order-service. Deploy dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, 2026-05-12T07:40Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and bumped the schema to v2. settlement-service, which expects schema v1 with 'qty', began failing to deserialize every OrderExecuted message at 07:42:14Z ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'), then treated the message as a poison message and retried it endlessly, blocking partition orders-3. As a result zero settlements posted and consumer_lag climbed from ~45 to 61605 by 09:45; the retry storm drove CPU to ~70%. The reported consumer poll-config change (cfg-3004, 07:35) is a coincidence/red herring: it cannot produce schema-mismatch errors, and the error onset tracks the order-service deploy. kafka and ledger-db are healthy, ruling out infrastructure/dependency causes. Fix: roll back or fix order-service v2.16.0 to emit schema v1-compatible events (or add settlement-service compatibility for v2), and skip/unblock the poisoned offset.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change broke settlement-service deserialization
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, 07:40) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and bumped the event schema to v2. settlement-service still expects schema v1 with 'qty', so every OrderExecuted message on partition orders-3 fails to deserialize; the consumer treats it as a poison message, retries endlessly and blocks the partition, so no settlements are posted and consumer lag grows unbounded.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 renames qty->quantity and sets schema header v2 on OrderExecuted
settlement-service expects schema v1 with 'qty' and fails deserialization
Poison message retried forever, blocking partition orders-3
No settlements posted; consumer lag climbs to 61605 by 09:45

assumptions: The 07:42 first error is caused by the first v2 OrderExecuted message after the 07:40 deploy
No consumer-side compatibility shim exists for schema v2

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer poll config change degraded throughput
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-3004 lowered consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 07:35, reducing batch throughput and letting lag accumulate. This is the change the reporter suspected.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: A smaller poll batch would slow consumption but cannot produce 'failed to deserialize ... missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' errors or poison-message partition blocking. The errors are the direct cause of zero settlements, and they begin 2 min after the order-service deploy, not the 07:35 config change. The config change alone is insufficient to explain the hard stop.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Infrastructure failure: Kafka partition reassignment / broker issue
ranked_hypotheses.statement: As in HIST-112, the consumer could have lost its partition assignment or hit a broker problem, causing lag to grow and settlements to stall.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: kafka logs show no errors (only 2 benign connection-reset WARNs) and no rebalance/reassignment events. The errors are explicit deserialization failures tied to a schema version mismatch, which a broker problem cannot produce.

facts.statement: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) deployed 07:40 renamed qty->quantity and added schema header v2 for OrderExecuted.
settlement-service began logging deserialization failures for OrderExecuted at 07:42:14Z citing missing 'qty' and schema v1 vs header v2.
The consumer then treated the message as poison and blocked partition orders-3, retrying endlessly.
CPU rose to ~70% while memory and DB pool stayed flat, consistent with a retry storm rather than resource exhaustion.
kafka and ledger-db showed no errors during the window.
settlement-service itself had no code deployments, so the fault originates upstream at order-service.

assumptions: The first v2 OrderExecuted message on orders-3 arrived shortly after the 07:40 deploy, producing the 07:42:14 error.
settlement-service has no runtime schema-v2 compatibility path.
order-service v2.16.0 was not rolled back by the time of this analysis (status 'live').
(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) settlement-service consumer_lag inflected in the 07:30-07:45 bucket and climbed to 61605 by 09:45.

timeline.event: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) deployed: OrderExecuted qty->quantity, schema header v2
First deserialization error in settlement-service ('missing required field qty ... header says v2')
Poison-message retries begin; partition orders-3 blocked
consumer_lag bucket jumps (avg 4829) and CPU rises to ~70%

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service dep-6010 (v2.16.0) to the previous version, or hotfix it to emit OrderExecuted in schema v1 (field 'qty') or dual-write compatible events.
recommended_actions.rationale: The v2 schema is incompatible with settlement-service's v1 deserializer and is the source of all failures.

recommended_actions.action: Unblock the poisoned offset: skip/seek past orders-3@8841207 or deploy a settlement-service fix that tolerates v2, then restart the consumer group.
recommended_actions.rationale: The retry loop on a single poison message is blocking the whole partition and prevents any settlement posting.

recommended_actions.action: Add schema-compatibility enforcement (contract tests / schema registry) between order-service producers and settlement-service consumers before future deploys.
recommended_actions.rationale: A field rename with a schema-version bump broke a downstream consumer; a registry would have caught this pre-deploy.

recommended_actions.action: Do not treat cfg-3004 (poll batch 500->200) as the cause; consider reverting only if throughput concerns remain after the schema fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: Evidence shows the config change cannot explain the schema-mismatch errors or the hard stop.

data_gaps: No direct consumer-group/partition-assignment telemetry was available to confirm the partition-blocked state beyond the app log messages.

No producer-side (order-service) metrics for event publish volume per schema version were available to size the backlog of v2 messages.
